questions.prompt: Put the stages a request goes through around model binding in order.
steps: Model binding maps request data to the action's parameters
questions.explanation: Routing must pick the action before its parameters can be bound, and binding has to produce values before validation can check them; only then does the action run.

questions.prompt: The client sends the request in the comment. What JSON does the action return?
options: `{ "id": 5, "name": null }`
`400 Bad Request`, because `name` is not in the route
questions.explanation: `id` matches the `{id}` route token, so it comes from `/5`; `name` is not in the route, so it is bound from the query string `?name=pen`.

questions.prompt: An action binds straight to a `Product` entity that has an `IsAdminOnly` property. What is the **overposting** risk?
options: The request body becomes too large to parse
A client can include `"isAdminOnly": true` and model binding sets that sensitive property automatically
The action is called twice for the same request
`IsAdminOnly` is always reset to `true`
questions.explanation: Overposting (mass assignment) happens because the binder fills every matching property, including ones a normal user should never be able to set.

questions.prompt: What does the lesson recommend as the real-world protection against overposting?
options: List the allowed fields with `[Bind("Name,Price")]` on every action
Validate the entity with `[Required]` on every property
Bind the entity from the query string instead of the body
Accept a DTO with only the client-settable fields and set sensitive values like `IsAdminOnly` on the server
questions.explanation: Rather than relying on `[Bind]` (hard to maintain) or exposing the entity, use a DTO such as `CreateProductDto`; the server builds the entity and controls `IsAdminOnly` itself.

questions.prompt: How many parameters of one action method can have `[FromBody]`?
options: Exactly two
At most one
As many as you like
None; `[FromBody]` only goes on properties
questions.explanation: `[FromBody]` binds from the request body using an input formatter, and an action method can have at most one parameter with this attribute.

questions.prompt: The custom `CommaSeparatedModelBinderProvider` is registered with `options.ModelBinderProviders.Insert(0, ...)`. Why index `0`?
options: Index `0` means the provider is disabled until it is enabled explicitly
Providers must always be added at index `0` or registration throws
It gives the provider the highest priority, so it is checked before the built-in providers
It makes the binder apply only to the first parameter of each action
questions.explanation: Inserting at the front of the provider list gives the custom provider the highest priority, so it gets the first chance to bind `List<int>` from `ids=1,2,3`.
